# 



# **OCTOBER 22, 2026**

** _ _****_IDEAS & INSIGHTS – IN BRIEF_**·         **MKT UPDATES –** Narrative
shift overnight amid geopolitics concerns; META first take from JPM Specialist
**Mark S****chilsky.** ·         **TRADE IDEA FROM JPM CREDIT TRADING (WILLIAM
JARVIS) –** J.P. Morgan AI Hyperscaler Baskets via 3-month TRS. If you would
like to receive to receive the full notes or trade with the team, please reach
out to them
here.·
**US MKT INTEL VIEW** – We are **Tactically Bullish** and update the
**Monetization Menu**. **_JPM MARKET INTEL MORNING UPDATE_** ·         **SPX
-1.1%, NDX -1.9%, RTY -0.9%.** WTI +238bps at $99.46, NatGas -86bps to $2.77,
UK NatGas +225bps to £2.2007, Gold -135bps to $4,085, Silver -353bps to
$55.92, 10Y @ 5.071%, and VIX @ 18.49.·         **US:** Futs are sharply
weaker with Tech lagging amid geopolitical risks and the resumption of the
tech selloff; oil added 2-3% on chatters over renewed Iran kinetic-risk post
US mid-term election
(NYT article “U.S. and Israel Draw Up Plans for
Renewed Strikes on Iran After Elections”). Tech was particularly weak with
META reversing its initial post-earnings gain over +5% to -2% pre-market now;
TSLA -5.2%, NVDA -2.4%. Yields down ~3–5bp across the curve (bull steepening)
as we resumed the flight-to-quality trade and was also driven by another spike
in French 10s. USD is softer (DXY ~-22bp). We saw a broad selloff across
multiple pockets of Cyclicals with defensives being the outperformer. ·
**EU/UK:** Major markets are lower with broad-based de-risking; SX5E and Italy
lagged. Thematically, Semis and Electrification are among the top
underperformers, while Defensives and Rate-sensitive baskets are the only ones
in the green. Rates are mixed: 10y Bunds -2bp and 10y Gilts -1bp, but France
is the stress point with 10Y yields +11bp to 5.12% driving a fresh high in
risk-premium. Beta/Momentum being sold with little rotation in other Cyclicals
sectors. UKX -0.6%, SX5E -1.8%, SXXP -1.1%, DAX -1.0%. CSI -1.8%, HSI -3.0%,
NKY -2.7%, ASX -0.4%, KOSPI -3.5%._ _**_CATALYSTS: TODAY AND WEEK AHEAD_** ·
**US MACRO DATA:** Initial/Continuing Jobless Claims and Initial Claims 4-Wk
Moving Avg at 8.30am ET. Leading Index at 10am ET. Kansas City Fed Mfg
Activity at 11am ET. [OCT 20-22] NVIDIA GTC Berlin·         **US EARNINGS:**
AAL, BE, **BX** , CBRE, CMCSA, COCO, CRS, DECK, DOW, HBAN, HON, LAZ, **LMT** ,
MXL, MSM, NDAQ, **NEM** , PCG, **PG** , POOL, ROP, THRM, TSCO, TTMI, **UNP** ,
VKTX, **VLO** , VRSN, **WDC** ·         **GLOBAL MACRO DATA:**(Japan) Machine
Tool Orders (revision) at 2am ET. (France) Mfg Confidence at 2.45am ET.
(Eurozone) Consumer Confidence at 10am ET. (UK) GfK Consumer Confidence at
7.01pm ET.**(Japan) CPI at 7.30pm ET. (Japan) PMIs at 8.30pm ET.****_
_****_JPM MARKET INTEL EQUITY & MACRO NARRATIVE_**Wednesday's session closed
near its highs: AI/Tech led and Momentum outperformed, while cyclical groups
such as machinery, banks, credit cards and hotels also rallied. **That tone
reversed overnight.** META first traded higher on its revenue beat and Q4
guide, but it has since given back those gains and is -1.9% pre-market. On the
headline level, the main catalyst was the chatters over renewed Iran kinetic-
risk post US mid-term election
(NYT article “U.S. and Israel Draw Up Plans for
Renewed Strikes on Iran After Elections”). However, underlying price actions
and feedback from our trading desk also suggested the still fragile narrative
around AI financing concerns and the lack of conviction / re-grossing from the
recent tech reversal (concerns about how AI spending gets financed are still
unresolved despite solid prints).  ·         **META EARNINGS FIRST TAKE (MARK
SCHILSKY)** – _[Mark published below immediately after the initial earnings
release]_ C You in January: META is currently trading up +3% after hours after
producing a Q3 result that I would characterize as inline with investor
expectations (+26% Y/Y FXN Revneue growth). The Q426 Revneue guide is
decidedly better than expected – and the high end of the range contemplates a
2-point FXN acceleration. That is VERY good. More importantly, Susan provided
some 2027 ‘guidance’ that will leave some investors wanting as we really got
nothing concrete on 2027 Opex or Capex. She did state: “Looking ahead,
although we are not providing a full-year 2027 revenue outlook, the benefits
our AI investments are delivering to the core business, combined with emerging
opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain
strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027.” Strong overall revenue growth
sounds good. But how strong? Finally, as leaked by Semafor before the close,
META is issuing non-voting C-Class shares to all shareholders in January which
will effectively become a 2:1 stock split. While I think this still means we
are likely to get an equity raise in the future, this would seem to suggest
that we won’t get one until early 2027. The overhang lives on! But the Q4
Revenue growth really is great. Focus on that.o   Q326 Earnings Results:§
Revenue of $64.6B grew +26% Y/Y reported & FXN. This is slightly better than
investor expectations which I characterized as ‘~$64B with a slight upward
bias.’ Call it inline.§  Ad Impressions grew +10% Y/Y. Ad Prices grew +14%
Y/Y.o   Q426/2026/2027 Guidance:§  Q426 Revenue was guided in the range of
$73B to $76B (+22% to +27% Y/Y reported – that’s +23% to +28% Y/Y FXN). This
is decidedly better than investor expectations of a guidance range of $72B to
$75B with the high end representing+25% Y/Y FXN growth. Put another way, the
high end of the guide is a 2-point acceleration! That’s a great number.o
2026 Opex was upped ~$10B due to the legal charges that we all knew were
coming. Call this inline. o   “At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs
losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion.”o   2026
Capex was upped at the lower end of the range by +$5B as expected. Now it’s
$135B to $145B. Again, inline.o   2027 ‘Guidance’: “Looking beyond 2026, we
are still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year, but we
expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business
and emerging AI initiatives. Our current capacity and what is scheduled to
come online gives us the flexibility to allocate resources across model
training, core business growth, and the development and support of new
products. Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental
advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and
more efficient monetization. Building on this progress, our MSL investments
are creating the technology and infrastructure needed to unlock significant
new revenue opportunities and strengthen capabilities across the business.
While these investments will take longer to generate returns than those in our
core business, the breadth of monetization opportunities and internal

**Call to action**|  We are updating estimates following Lam’s Sep-Q (1QFY27)

**HIGHLIGHTS**|  Management’s commentary on 2027 WFE was constructive and
points to accelerating growth, but near-term supply chain execution remains a
concern. Key component shortages are being compounded by broad-based vendor
price increases aimed at margin expansion. Even so, we believe the supply
chain can currently support ~$200B of WFE, with enough lead time over the next
year to expand capacity toward $300B. Customers' commitment will be the key
factor. We expect SCE customers to begin committing to 2028 system deliveries,
giving the supply chain the visibility it needs to invest and scale to support
$300B of WFE.  
---  
|

  * .LRCX's Sep-Q results beat expectations, driven by strength in systems and operating execution. Revenue of $8.22B (+22% Q/Q, +54% Y/Y) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.20 were records, with margins above the guidance midpoints and operating cash flow roughly double the Street. December guidance calls for revenue of $8.6B (+/- $400M), though supply constraints are pushing some systems shipments into the March quarter.
  * Management's initial CY27 WFE view of at least $200B is still gated by component availability, and the company expects to refine it next quarter as visibility improves on fab schedules, industry readiness, and supply chain availability.
  * Lam continues to frame rising etch and deposition intensity as the main reason it can outgrow WFE, supported by advanced packaging, foundry/logic, DRAM, and eventually a fuller NAND recovery.
  * China was 35% of revenue, helped by both domestic and multinational customers. It is expected to be meaningfully lower sequentially in December, as domestic China customers decline while multinationals there stay reasonably strong.
  * NAND upgrades still have room to run through 2027, though customer scheduling can slow the pace in a high-demand environment. Management sees the next upgrade cycle and more specialized AI-oriented NAND demand extending the opportunity, and Lam is positioned for both upgrades and any future capacity additions.

  
---  
|

  * The 70% advanced packaging growth outlook for this year is unchanged, with further growth expected next year. Panel-level packaging is still in the beginning stages. Management sees it as a logical fit for larger packages and expects it to take a meaningful share of packaging work over time. Mature-node spending outside China is not expected to grow meaningfully in 2026, but is expected to be strong in 2027.

It is becoming increasingly clear that Meta's investments in AI are yielding
ever increasing returns for advertisers, which in turn is supporting not only
top-line durability, but, in fact, advertising revenue growth acceleration.
Moreover, by leveraging LLM oriented AI infrastructure, Instagram and Facebook
hit all-time-highs in engagement, while the company's ad systems continued to
drive conversion improvements supporting monetization efficiency. Importantly,
we think these are still in the very early innings and should prove durable
drivers of topline growth for the foreseeable future. **We also contend that
Meta is increasingly in a transition period whereby compute will pivot from
being perceived as a "cost center" to being viewed as a "revenue driving
asset."** Of course, this has already been on display within the FoA segment,
but as we look ahead to 2027/2028 it appears that the combination of Muse,
Enterprise (API & Muse Code), and Business Agent monetization could become
growing revenue drivers, for which the contribution will scale with Meta's
access to compute (and ability to improve compute efficiency). To that end,
with the large fixed training costs for the SOTA models complete, it appears
focus is shifting to serve the scaling high-margin inference demand. Of
course, there continue to be concerns around the magnitude of these
investments and the potential for dilutive external funding, however, as
adoption and monetization of these products ramp, there may be a growing
number of willing funding parters that likely see Meta as well-positioned to
penetrate the large consumer agent TAM, capture the SMB business agent
opportunity and potentially make inroads in enterprise as well. Notably, these
are all complementary to the base business, which is also leveraging Meta's
growing infrastructure to accelerate growth.All in all, Meta's capital
investments are having strong returns in terms of engagement and ad
performance, which is translating to Meta's current durable advertising
revenue growth. This is simultaneously affording Meta the ability to launch
its suite of agents (business and consumer) that are scaling in adoption,
while also becoming a leading player on the frontier with optionality within
hardware. Bigger picture: Muse is showing unusually strong early commercial
intent and will monetize earlier than Meta's traditional product playbook.
Business Agents potentially connect 3.6bn consumers with a 500mn-business
ecosystem. Enterprise provides another potentially high-margin destination for
the same inference infrastructure. **_Given this mix of near-term tailwinds,
alongside longer-term strategic advances (with ample greenfield
opportunities), we believe Meta deserves a valuation multiple at least on par
with the peers, if not higher._**  As such, we maintain our Buy Rating and are
raising our target price to $840 from $820, which is based on a 27x P/E

**| 1| NOKIA (Buy + 68%) - So Far So Good - We Expect Further Upgrades To Come
- ****IP + Optical to Accelerate to 25-30% in
2027******

Nokia's Q3-26 sales and comparable gross margin were slightly ahead of
expectations. The comparable operating margin of 11.7% is well ahead (JEFe
8.9%) with the beat mainly in Mobile Infrastructure (14.5% vs JEFe 9.5%).

This was helped by a pull-forward of revenue from Q4 to Q3. IP Networks
revenue grew 43% YoY, which we believe reflects a further acceleration in
Switch sales to Google.

Optical Networks grew 18% YoY, broadly in-line with previous quarters given
capacity constraints. AI+Cloud orders sales were up 123% YoY, with orders of
€1.5bn in the quarter.

The order decline from €2.8bn in Q2 is estimated to have come mainly from IP
Networks.

**Nokia now expects IP+Optical in 2026 to grow somewhat above its 18-20%
guidance, with the upside likely to be from IP Networks.**

It has also guided IP+Optical to grow at 25-30% in 2027 (JEFe 25.3%),
reflecting confidence in the fab ramp, orders and supply.

**Despite the strong 2027 guide, we see scope for further upgrades in coming
quarters.**

**Q3-26 Results:**

• Revenue €5154m (cons. at €5057m, JEFe at €5103m).

• Comp. gross margin 44.6% (cons. at 44.1%, JEFe at 44.3%).

• Comp. operating margin 11.7% (cons. at 9.0%, JEFe at 8.9%).

• Diluted EPS €0.09 (cons. at €0.07, JEFe at €0.07).

• FY-26 guidance: comparable operating profit of between €2.1bn-€2.6bn (cons
at €2.4bn, JEFe at €2.5bn).

Divisions:

• Network Infrastructure sales €2158m, 17% YoY (cons. at €2173m, JEFe at
€2146m); Operating margin 10.0% (cons. at 10.0%, JEFe at 9.8%).

• Mobile Infrastructure sales €2902m, 5% YoY (cons. at €2778m, JEFe at
€2854m); Operating margin 14.5% (cons. at 10.1%, JEFe at 9.5%).

• Portfolio businesses' sales €96m, -1% YoY (cons. at €105m, JEFe at €100m);
Operating margin 3.1% (cons. at -0.9%, JEFe at 14.5%).

** **

**| 2| SAP \- Backs Up The Recent Share Price Move**

3Q26 numbers from SAP are undeniably strong and our first impression is that
this is a clean quarter of better than expected numbers in all dimensions.

With the conf call calling out AI as a driver of strong momentum (AI and BDC
was included in 90% of the top 50 deals), disruption narratives are starting
to get knocked down.

The shares have been strong into the print, but we see no reason for the trend
to reverse.

**Key headlines:** This is the cleanest quarter of outperformance from SAP
that we can recall for some time, with all dimensions of orders (CCB), cloud
revenues, group revenues, and EBIT beating expectations.

Starting with the current cloud backlog (CCB), SAP has reported 26% growth, in
line with the 2Q26 run rate. Consensus was expecting a slight fade to 25%, but
this was a bar that had drifted up from 24% in mid-September.

As a result, this will be seen as a strong result that starts to de-risk FY26
and, to some extent, FY27.

**P &L beats:** While the CCB is arguably the most important metric, this has
also been supported with a stronger P&L. **Cloud revenue growth came in at 25%
in cc, 2% ahead of consensus** , albeit the call referenced 1ppt was
attributed to one-off benefits from clients returning from distress.
Meanwhile, Cloud and Software growth grew 14% YoY, 1% ahead of cons and total
group revenue growth of 12% was also 1% ahead. After accounting for FX
impacts, the actuals versus cons are shown in Chart 1.

Lower down the P&L, EBIT beat by 2% which will be seen as reassuring after the
2Q26 margin pressures. This implies 3Q26 opex which is broadly similar to 2Q
and in line with cons.

The one number that will cause some debate is cloud gross margin, with 3Q26
numbers falling 70bps YoY, and 30bps sequentially versus 2Q26. However, in the
context of the overall print, we do not expect investors to fixate on this
issue.

**Guidance:** FY26 guidance ranges are left unchanged. However, SAP now
caveats that it expects cloud revenue towards the upper end of the 23-25%
range and similarly cloud and software revenue towards the upper end of the
12-13% range. EBIT guidance is unchanged at €11.8-12bn, which reflects the
higher opex that has been creeping into the P&L. After accounting for FX, cons
is aligned with the mid-point of the EBIT range.

Importantly, the strong order intake will start to lift spirits looking into
4Q26 and FY27 and comments on the call suggested 4Q26 CCB could hit 24% at the
high end. There were plenty of caveats on the call which suggests we shouldn't
get too complacent about the outlook but this sort of CCB scenario quickly
starts to underpin FY27 expectations.

The shares have performed well ahead of the results but, based on our
interactions, it remains under-owned and we see no reason why the shares won't
respond positively to a strong print.



**| 3| META \- Capex Supportive ?**

"Company also raised their 2026E opex outlook by $10bn to **$175-179bn** ,
mostly to reflect legal charges (vs prior $165-169bn, expects $165-169bn), and
capex guide by $5bn at the low-end to **$135-145bn** (vs prior $130-145bn,
street at $142bn) – both generally in-line with expects. No formal guide for
2027E, but in the press release they said they “ _expect to continue investing
aggressively_ to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives” –
note that buyside expects for 2027E into the print were at $215-220bn/$260bn+
for opex/capex (vs consensus at $204bn/~$200bn). "

**We think the midpoint increase from $137.5bn to $140bn is not that
meaningful and probably only reflects DRAM price increases etc. However, if
the 2027 guide is where the buyside expects it to be at $260bn, that would be
pretty positive.  **

 “we are quite early in developing our budget and capacity plans for next
year. So, we are, I would say, at the point where we are both investing --
sorry, evaluating a lot of investment proposals that have attractive return
profiles over different time horizons, and we want to figure out how we can
fund as many of those as possible within the construct of our overall budget
and financial goals. But it's very dynamic, and it's still pretty early. And
so we don't have anything more specific or quantitative to share until we get
to the Q4 call, which is typically when we share guidance for the next year.”

** **

**_More Detail_**

**Meta (META US,BUY,TP $875)** fading in the after market, now only up +2% vs
as high as +7% – 3Q revs of **$64.6bn** beat us/street’s $63.4bn/$63.3bn and
buyside’s ~$64bn bogey, while 4Q rev guide of **$73-76bn** also beat vs
us/street’s $74.3bn/$73.6bn and bogeys of $75bn on the high-end. Company also
raised their 2026E opex outlook by $10bn to **$175-179bn** , mostly to reflect
legal charges (vs prior $165-169bn, expects $165-169bn), and capex guide by
$5bn at the low-end to **$135-145bn** (vs prior $130-145bn, street at $142bn)
– both generally in-line with expects. No formal guide for 2027E, but in the
press release they said they “ _expect to continue investing aggressively_ to
support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives” – note that
buyside expects for 2027E into the print were at $215-220bn/$260bn+ for
opex/capex (vs consensus at $204bn/~$200bn). For Reality Labs, mgmt also
guided for losses to narrow to -$15bn next year (better than current
consensus’s -$20bn), and also announced a new class of non-voting Class C
shares to provide flexibility for future capital raising (14C filing hit the
tape around ~40mins before market close, link
here).
Brent’s first take is
here.



On the earnings call, no real color on 2027E either (only guide they gave was
“strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027”, mainly driven by ads but also
some small incremental contribution from AI), and Susan made it clear that
there were “no specific financing plans to announce at this time” – though
perhaps the Class C share announcement implies that any fundraising is more
likely to come after Jan.



**But mgmt shared some +ve initial metrics for Muse and enterprise, and did a
good job outlining the longer term monetization opportunities and
profitability:**

  * Muse
    * **10mn+** users in US/Canada in 1st 1.5 months of launch
    *  _Engagement and retention “off to a strong start”,_ with **_25%_**_of people who set up Muse using it daily ( >2x level of Threads initially), with retention improving the longer they use it_
    *  _Shopping/commerce is the #1 use case, and**25%+** of WAU’s engaging in shopping, with avg purchase size of **$200+**_
    * _Expect to improve compute cost efficiency by**> 10x** in the next year_, which will enable Muse to be profitable once rev is at scale
    * Avg rev per US user for existing Family of Apps users currently at several hundred dollars annually, _expect Muse will reach an even higher level over time due to level of commerce activity_
    * 3 main business models: 1) commerce take rate; 2) subscription for advanced models or extra tokens; 3) ads upside from connecting to other surfaces across **META**
    *  _Expect to work on monetization of Muse sooner vs normal playbook with other products in the past_
  * Enterprise
    * Main enterprise offering in the near term is the model API, Muse Code, business agents – all growing quickly
    * Over time, want to have a whole business network of Muse agents – higher dimension of proactivity can be unlocked with consumer agents and business agents interacting together, which will enable more transactions and activity to happen
    * See significant opportunity to extend Muse to the 500mn+ small businesses currently using **META** ’s Family of Apps 
    * Expect businesses of all sizes will use AI agents across software development, productivity, sales, marketing, customer service, and enterprise to be a new diversified recurring revenue stream



**_Initial feedback is +ve_** – **bulls** were impressed by the top line beat,
with the ads business showing more resilience than anyone expected (and with
plenty of runway to improve/accel further), and that mgmt articulated the
monetization pathway for Muse and enterprise quite well. In particular,
**META** highlighting shopping/commerce (including travel) as the #1 use case
for Muse, with avg purchase size of $200+, was quite interesting – and could
pressure some of the ecommerce/OTA names tomorrow. **Bears** push back saying
that there weren’t any huge surprise this Q, and that the commentary around
Muse was good but generally in-line with expectations. More importantly,
market was looking for this Q as a potential clearing event in terms of
clarity around a capital raise, and we didn’t get it – so stock likely to get
faded as this will continue to be an overhang on the stock in coming months,
and as investors remain generally uncertain around 2027E #’s given limited
color/direction on opex/capex today.



Sentiment on **META** has done a 180 since last Q, rallying ~30% from the last
print – HF’s turned long mostly after the initial success with Muse, the
latest Muse Wonder model releases bringing **META** to becoming competitive at
the frontier, and rising expectations on Enterprise after the hiring of
ex-**MDB** CEO CJ Desai (link
here), but LO’s likely still mostly EW. In recent weeks,
positioning likely lightened up a bit (though still a long lean), with fast
money trimming/taking profits on 1) initial Muse hype fading, and concerns on
adoption plateauing with many internet/e-commerce sites blocking Muse and
other AI agents; 2) worries about a step-up in capex given the increased
compute needs from Muse; 3) potential fundraising risks. Think a potential
equity raise still will remain the biggest impediment for people to pile into
**META** on the long side, even if things are sound pretty great
fundamentally.



**_Key takeaways from earnings call_**

  * **Outlook**
    * Revs
      * 4Q $73-76bn – 1pp FX headwind
    * Expenses
      * 2026 $175-179bn, reflecting $9.9bn legal charge
    * Capex
      * 2026 $135-145bn (tightened from $130-145bn)

    * Current capacity and what is scheduled to come online gives us flexibility to allocate resources across model training, core business growth, development support of new products
    * Expect to sustain strong overall rev growth throughout 2027
      * Feeling good about budgets investments in core ads and engagement initiatives next year
      * New AI businesses can also begin contributing incremental revs in 2027, and can scale meaningfully over time
      * Near-term focus is on building high quality products, achieving scaled product market fit
      * Feel good that AI is going to become a meaningful source of revenue diversification over time
    * Reality Labs losses to narrow next to $15bn
    * No specific financing plans to announce at this time
  * **AI**
    * Muse
      * Initial position very strong
      * In 1.5 months, 10mn+ people in US/Canada set up Muse personal agents
      * #1 in App Store almost every day
      * Engagement retention off to strong start
        * 25% of people who set up Muse use it on any given day
        * For earliest adopters, the longer that they use Muse, the better retention seems to get
        * This is >2x the level that Threads started at
      * Use cases
        * Shopping – most common use case
          * 25%+ of weekly actives engaging in shopping, avg purchase size >$200 
            * Includes travel – but travel also another top use case for Muse
          * Plaid said they hadn’t seen activity on any connector
          * Worked with Stripe to raise credit limits
        * Personal productivity
        * Creativity
        * Email, calendar
      * Muse Wonder improving quality engagement and retention further
      * Entering new phase to scale Muse
        * Scale the product
          * Want to create large scale user network as quickly as possible
          * Family of Apps avg rev per US user is several hundreds of dollars annually – expect Muse to reach a higher level over time
        * Grow revenue
          * Most people will get the product free, and will build commerce tools and get paid transaction fee, which will be paid by businesses
          * For people who want most advanced models or use extra tokens, can subscribe directly and pay
          * For those who want Muse to help improve personalization and quality of content and ads across Meta, they can connect those experiences as well
          * Will work on monetization of Muse sooner vs normal playbook, given:
            * Size of the numbers, in terms of costs and opportunities
            * Commerce being a large part of what people do – able to charge take rate
              * Includes Travel, which is another top use case
          * Not charging people upfront for Muse, because want to establish Muse network
        * Optimize compute costs
          * Total servicing costs to rise
          * Expect to improve compute cost efficiency by >10x in the next year, driven by better utilization of off-peak capacity, more efficient models, and inference optimization – which will enable it to be profitable once rev is at scale
          * Since training is a large fixed cost, now with leading models, want to serve as much high margin inference demand as possible
            * Hence building Meta Enterprise Platform 
            * Multiple ways to deploy advanced models, increasing changes that one or more significantly outperforms expectations
          * AI models self improvement will also help improve software efficiency 
      * No limit on how effectively we can use Muse Wonder to improve core business – expect an increasing rate of improvement 
      * One of the biggest constraints so far – due to compute intensiveness, have not launched globally
        * 10mn users already in 1st 6 weeks from US/Canada only – would expect # to be significantly larger if rolled out to more markets
        * But have to do the work to bring efficiency in line to make a global rollout make sense
      * Compute efficiency work is important – building enough compute to be able to serve a billion plus people
      * Also need to build business around it 
      * And continuing to increase value of product thru continuing development of new models
        * Rolled out to Muse Spark initially – default for free tier now
        * Muse Wonder now available in paid tier, and working on getting a more efficient version more broadly
      * Overwhelmingly, businesses are very excited about enabling this – new opportunity to increase sales and quality of experience for existing customers, and potentially bring in new customers
      * Across the business ecosystem, different people will adopt at difference paces
      * But overall, have been positively surprised by how quickly a huge amount of businesses have wanted to figure out how Muse can use their services more effectively, and have reached out to us to integrate it
      * Not everyone wants to be an early adopter, and will work with those on terms that makes sense for them
      * Many business excited to partner with us, and some businesses understandably focused on protecting customer relationships
      * Expect the market to ultimately evolve away from agents attempting to navigate every digital experience like a human, and will move towards more permission structured interactions, including authenticated API’s, approved agent partnerships, or direct communications between a consumer’s personal agent and business’s own agent
      * Helping establish new industry standards like personal agent protocol
      * Expect adoption to be uneven and will take time
    * Enterprise
      * See significant opportunity extend Muse to small businesses – currently 500mn+ use META’s Family of Apps to reach customers and generate revenue
        * Acquiring customers, operating more efficiently, helping people complete transactions
      * The main enterprise offering in the near term is the model API, Muse Code, business agents – all growing quickly

      * Many people using Muse today to help run small businesses – automating parts of setting up a small business
      * Also another version of Muse for corporate environments
      * Building a Muse network where agents will talk to each other
      * Will have a very valuable boost in the utility for consumers too
      * AI creating huge amount of disruption in enterprise today – traditional enterprise companies don’t have this locked down yet
      * Expects businesses of all sizes will use AI agents across software development, productivity, sales, marketing, customer service
      * Expect it to be a new diversified recurring revenue stream

## Record Results / In-Line Guide; Supply Constraints Taking Hold; CY27 WFE
Outlook of >$200B Keeps Bigger Picture Constructive; Reit OW

LRCX, LRCX US  
Price (21 Oct 26):$260.81  
Price Target (Dec-27):$340.00  
  
Lam Research Corporation (LRCX) delivered solid F1Q results with revenues,
GMs, OPMs, and non-GAAP EPS all reaching record levels and coming in above
consensus expectations. However, the out-quarter revenue and EPS guide for F2Q
was largely in-line with Street expectations and modestly below the buyside
estimates we heard coming into the print. Management guided F2Q revenues to
$8.60B ± $400M, implying ~5% Q/Q growth off a record base, with GMs of 52.5%,
OPMs of 40.5%, and EPS of $2.33 at the midpoint. The guide embeds continued
strength across memory, leading-edge F/L, advanced packaging, and CSBG, but is
being capped by near-term supply-chain constraints (as we had highlighted in
our 3Q26 Sector
Outlook) and a meaningful step down in domestic China revenue after a
very strong F1Q (China ~35% of sales). Based on our checks, these constraints
appear to be tied to more general components (e.g., gas delivery subsystems,
etc.) rather than anything LRCX-specific. Management also noted that the out-
quarter revenue guide would have been “a bit higher” absent supply
constraints, and that shipments delayed by supply constraints should move into
the Mar-qtr, suggesting the issue is timing/supply-related as opposed to any
weakness in underlying demand. As it relates to this, LRCX also raised its
CY26 WFE to the mid-$150B range and (surprisingly) introduced a preliminary
CY27 WFE outlook of >$200B, which implies ~30% Y/Y growth (with growth
continuing to be led by DRAM, leading-edge F/L, and NAND). All told, although
the out-quarter guide might have been softer than some investors had hoped, we
believe the overarching picture remains constructive as customer demand
remains strong, revenues delayed by supply constraints should move into the
Mar-qtr (F3Q27), and management’s preliminary CY27 WFE outlook of >$200B
reinforces the strength and durability of the current WFE upcycle. We continue
to see LRCX outgrowing broader WFE on rising deposition/etch intensity, NAND
upgrades, advanced packaging, and CSBG momentum, while profitability continues
to reset higher with OPMs now above ~40% and a path toward mid-50% GMs. As
such, we view the aftermarket weakness as more reflective of elevated buyside
expectations than any deterioration in fundamentals. Reiterate $340 PT and OW-
rating.

  * F1Q27 (Sep-Qtr) results came in above Street estimates driven by robust spending across NAND, leading-edge F/L, and DRAM… LRCX reported solid F1Q27 results, with record revenues of $8.22B (+22% Q/Q, +54% Y/Y), coming in above the midpoint of the prior guide (~$8.10B) and JPM / Street estimates (~$8.10B / $8.13B). Memory continued to account for 46% of Systems revenues, with NAND rising to ~26% of Systems revenue on continued 256-layer+ conversions, while DRAM was ~20% of Systems revenue and reached a record dollar level on continued 1-alpha/1-beta/1-gamma spending tied to DDR5, LPDDR5, and HBM. Foundry also reached record levels at ~46% of Systems revenue, with growth being driven by leading-edge nodes, advanced packaging, and mature-node China demand. Logic accounted for the remaining ~8% of Systems revenues (down slightly from ~10% last quarter). In CSBG (the services business), LRCX delivered the fourth consecutive record quarter at nearly $2.49B (+40% Y/Y). As for other financial metrics, GMs reached a record ~52.4% and OPMs reached a record ~40.2%, which altogether resulted in a non-GAAP EPS of $2.20, above Street expectations at $2.15.

  * F2Q27 guide largely in-line with Street estimates and below buyside expectations… LRCX guided Dec-Qtr revenue to $8.60B ± 400M, which implies continued sequential growth (+4.6% Q/Q) off a record F1Q27 base, albeit with a meaningful deceleration relative to the prior 2 quarters (LRCX revenues grew +15% Q/Q in F4Q26 and +22% Q/Q in F1Q27). The out-quarter revenue guide also came in largely in-line with Street estimates ($8.60B) and below the buyside expectations we had heard from clients coming into the print. Management noted the revenue guide would have been “a bit higher” if not for near-term supply chain constraints, and indicated that constrained shipments should move into the March quarter. China notably represented 35% of F1Q revenues (on strong mature-node F/L demand), but is expected to be meaningfully lower next quarter (F2Q), driven by a decline in domestic China customers (while multinational China demand should remain reasonably strong). On other measures, LRCX guided GMs to 52.5% ± 1%, OPMs to 40.5% ± 1%, and non-GAAP EPS to $2.33 ± 0.15, with the EPS guide also coming in below the buyside estimates we had screened heading into results. 

  * CY26 WFE raised yet again, with LRCX issuing a preliminary CY27 WFE outlook of >$200B (+30%+ Y/Y)... LRCX once again raised its CY26 WFE outlook to the mid-$150B range, up from the low-$150B range last quarter and ~$140B range from earlier in the year. More importantly, management provided a preliminary CY27 WFE outlook of >$200B (one-quarter ahead of when the company typically outlines the out-year WFE), with growth being led by DRAM, leading-edge F/L, and NAND. Management noted that cleanroom space and certain component supply constraints are likely to limit customers’ and equipment suppliers’ ability to fully meet end demand in 2027, suggesting underlying demand could be even stronger. Including the Dec-Qtr guide, LRCX expects CY26 Systems revenue to grow well over 40% Y/Y (we model ~47% Y/Y), marking the company’s third consecutive year of WFE outperformance.

  * Maintaining PT at $340 on new 2027 exit-rate EPS of $12.35… On the back of tonight’s results, we are raising our CY26 / CY27 estimates to incorporate management's out-quarter guidance and its longer-term commentary on WFE. Our PT assumes that LRCX trades at ~27.5x our exit-rate CY27 EPS of $12.35, with the multiple standing towards the higher end of its comparable large-cap global semicap peers (24 - 28x).

# Meta Platforms Inc

## Muse Agent & Enterprise Paths Taking Shape; Reiterate Overweight & $940 PT

  
---  
  
By Doug Anmuth
AC,
Margaret
Hoffman,
Daniel
Pfeiffer

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
META, META US  
Price (21 Oct 26):$697.52  
**▲** Price Target (Dec-27):$940.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$920.00  
  
Meta delivered solid 3Q results with upside across revenue (+26% Y/Y),
operating income (~$23B & 35.4% margin ex the litigation legal charge), and
EPS ($7.40 ex the charge). The 4Q revenue outlook of $73B-$76B was also $1B
above our expectation at the high end as the core advertising business
continues to show strong growth, backed by AI ad improvements and video.
Importantly, this was the first quarter where MSL investments and Meta's
vision for personal superintelligence were met w/early product momentum across
Muse Wonder, the Muse AI agent, and enterprise opportunities in Meta Model API
& Muse Code. Muse is off to a strong start, w/10M people signed up in the US &
Canada, w/25% of those visiting daily. Shopping & travel are frequent use
cases, & current users (early adopters) are high ARPU users across the Family
of Apps. We're encouraged by healthy early engagement & retention, & note that
more than 500M businesses use Meta products, creating a distribution pipeline
for agentic adoption, & ultimately monetization. Meta expects to monetize Muse
primarily through a take-rate or outcome-based model, w/heavy users also
paying for subscriptions. Given that Muse is compute-intensive & the revenue
opportunity quite large, Meta indicated that it will work toward monetization
sooner than it typically has w/other new products. Pushback around the quarter
will likely come in 2 areas: First, Meta would not comment on 2027 total
expenses or capex, indicating that it's still working through the 2027 budget.
Ironically, Meta provided less color on next year's capex than it did just 3
months ago. Second, Meta is establishing a new class of non-voting Class C
stock, effective in January 2027. The new share class will come as a one-time
dividend in what is effectively a 2-for-1 stock split which helps preserve
Mark's voting control, and it is very similar to what Google introduced in
2014. All of that's fine, but investors are also focused on the 14C filing
details which suggest Meta has discussed an equity raise & recapitalization
for at least the last several months, and the possibility that Mark could sell
a meaningful amount of shares to cover liabilities if CA's Prop 40 wealth tax
were to pass. While it has been well known, the filing also discusses
management's view that it needs to raise hundreds of billions of dollars over
the next several years, all of which would seem to make an equity raise in
4Q26/1Q27 all the more likely. The sooner the better in our view as it would
remove the overhang and the Street now knows it will have non-voting shares in
Jan'27, and Meta can still do a substantial equity raise before then without
even coming close to impacting Mark's voting control. Net/net, some near-term
noise in Meta shares, but we're encouraged by core Advertising and Meta’s
outlook for strong overall revenue growth in 2027, and the path to
superintelligence is increasingly clear w/the Muse series of models &
products. Our estimates increase modestly as we now model 2027 revenue growth
of 23%, total expenses of $217B, capex of $255B, and 2028 GAAP EPS of $35.73.
We reiterate our Overweight rating & our $940 PT is based on 26x 2028E GAAP
EPS of $35.73.

  * AI-Driven Engagement & Ad Monetization Gains Continue. 3Q Ad revenue grew +26% Y/Y reported & FXN driven by AI-related engagement and monetization improvements, with impressions +10% Y/Y and pricing +14% Y/Y. 3Q global time spent per user reached an all-time high on IG and grew a DD% Y/Y and on FB Reels, time spent reached an all-time high globally and in the U.S., growing DD% Y/Y. Meta continues to simplify campaign creation & management for advertisers, with 10M+ small businesses using at least one AI creative tool in 3Q (vs. 9M+ in 2Q), and advertiser adoption of Meta’s video generation features grew 25% Q/Q. Additionally, advertisers who adopted Meta AI business assistant recommendations drove ~5% more coversions at the same cost per conversion, and increased their spend 9% vs. non-adopters. While advances in ads ranking & recommendation models have supported revenue growth, Meta believes there is headroom to continue improving recommendation initiatives and monetization efficiency, with Mark noting that Meta has not yet found the limit of how effectively compute can be applied to accelerate its own core business. Meta is also continuing to make progress on monetizing engagement beyond ads, with its unified Meta One subscription, which has surpassed 15M subscriptions and trials to date. 
  * Early Adoption of Muse is Strong. More than 10M people in the U.S. and Canada have set up Muse agents, with 25% of users using it daily, more than twice the level at which Threads started. The most common use case is shopping (25% of users) with average purchase sizes of over $200, followed by use of connectors such as email and calendar. Meta believes that Muse would otherwise have a much larger user base if it wasn’t so compute intensive, which is why Muse has yet to launch globally. As such, Meta’s primary focus is to improve compute efficiency and in tandem, work on scaling monetization sooner than its typical playbook which first starts with scaling engagement. Meta expects to improve cost efficiency by more than 10x over the next year, driven by better utilization of off-peak capacity, more efficient models, and inference optimization. The Muse revenue model has not changed from prior disclosures, with the primary focus being on making the product free for most users and generating revenue from a fee on transactions that Muse facilitates.
  * Meta is Equipped to Capture the Enterprise Opportunity. Meta has put a well-respected leader at the helm of its enterprise business with former MongoDB CEO CJ Desai. At his disposal is a frontier model in Muse Wonder coupled with 500M businesses that are using Meta’s products today. This positions Meta to bring together the models, infrastructure, global distribution, and longstanding relationships with businesses to offer model API access and Muse Code, driving subscription and usage-based revenue.

| | | We attended Nvidia's GTC Berlin this week, and come away with ongoing conviction that the company continues to effectively manage challenges in supply chain, land/power/shell, and funding - and even benefit from those challenges; reiterate OW/Top Pick in semis.   
---  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Focus on supply chain, with substantial long term commitment on substrates (adding SEMCO), expansions in CoWoS, and commitment for test capacity 
  * "DSX POD" has an understated importance; could lead to dramatic improvement in bring-up times, which can significantly improve cash flows of a neocloud 
  * The market is reacting to concerns around supply chain, land power shell, and funding - we remain convinced that all 3 aspects are opportunities for NVDA 
  * Reiterate OW, $300 target, Top Pick in semis 

  
  
No big surprises, but NVIDIA continues to add to its considerable advantages
heading into 2027. The Vera Rubin cycle is starting to pick up steam, though
we didn't get some of the details we might have expected on next year's Rubin
Ultra. But with demand remaining very strong, the focus is on closing the gap
between CY27 revenue guidance of 70%, and demand growth which mgmt has
characterized as 100%. To that end, the supply chain additions on substrate,
packaging and test, are an important bit of blocking and tackling. We continue
to see the biggest bottleneck as TSMC 3 nm wafers, which could free up over
time.

The DSX POD, detailed below, won't get the attention of more technology
oriented announcements, but could be an important differentiator. We see
NVIDIA's advantage coming from higher tokens per GW vs. competitors, but have
also found the arguments that NVIDIA provides faster bring-up time, longer
mean time between failure, and longer asset life than competing products as
very compelling. DSX POD deals with the bring-up time, reducing months of wait
time before assets can become productive by providing references for ODMs to
build completely functional clusters than can be brought up very rapidly. This
directly speaks to the cash flow issues of neoclouds, which will be able to
reduce the time that assets are unproductive which could help bridge funding
concerns.

Details from Jensen's keynote presentation: Nvidia usually opts to discuss the
most relevant product announcements at its flagship GTC in March, limiting the
amount of new color on the roadmap around the event. However, we did hear key
updates in terms of Nvidia's product momentum outside of the core business
(software, PCs, physical AI), and Nvidia's role in alleviating LPS constraints
with DSX, DSX POD, and DSX MaxLPS, and continued Rubin leadership in terms of
tokens per watt and tokens per dollar, both contributing to ongoing excitement
about the company's strategic positioning.

The Nvidia DSX POD is a new reference design for Vera Rubin systems built
inside modular containers, with integration and validation occurring before
delivery. That streamlines the deployment process, allowing the customer to
take delivery and begin producing tokens in days vs several months. The new
form factor can help improve working capital cycles for their customers, and
extend Nvidia's platform advantage with a quicker time to first token. The DSX
POD is part of the broader DSX AI factory reference architecture, where during
the keynote we heard about MaxLPS allowing customers to use 30% less power
with no change in token output. Nvidia will have 10+ customers in Europe
adopting the DSX platform for Vera Rubin AI factories.

Nvidia is also releasing new software for agentic AI safety, the OpenShell
Reference Architecture. OpenShell is an open-source framework built on Linux
that keeps each AI agent in its own sandbox and limits what it can access.
Nvidia Sentry, which runs on BlueField-4, adds a second layer that monitors
agents from outside the system. Management said most major frontier labs, OS
vendors, and security companies have adopted it, and Nvidia is working with an
AI lab on OpenShell agents. For Nvidia, it extends its content in agent
deployments beyond Rubin GPUs to Vera CPUs and BlueField-4.

Nvidia's AI RAN initiative continues to make progress, Nvidia made the first
commercial phone call on T-Mobile’s network with Nokia on CUDA, after roughly
eight years of work, with AI to be layered on top. Jensen talked to ~100,000
sites and ~100 GW of distributed telco base stations and data centers
eventually becoming distributed AI infrastructure.

As far as autonomous vehicles, four more brands will be Hyperion-compatible,
which supports Nvidia’s push to make Hyperion the industry-standard autonomous
vehicle architecture, which will eventually be connected to ride-hailing
networks. In humanoids, Nvidia is launching Agile ONE SN, a reference humanoid
built with Agile Robots, shipping preassembled with compute and software in 1Q
next year.

Separately from the keynote, Nvidia announced new plans for further capacity
expansion in substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines. In
substrates the combination of IBIDEN, SEMCO, and Unimicron will 2.5x capacity
over the next three years. Amkor plans to expand CoWoS-R wafer capacity by
more than 300% by the end of 2028 to support growth across CPUs and LPUs. In
the back-end Nvidia has committed a $1.1bn capacity reservation to support
KYEC's new US facilities and equipment, with HVM expected in April 2027.
Nvidia expects its total semi test capacity to 2x from 2026 to 2027. In CPO
SPIL's expansion targets a 15x increase by mid-2027, with expectations for
another 2x by the end of 2028. Read

primary.article_text: Press Release Share Tweet Twitter Share LinkedIn Share Facebook Email ic_arrow-back-to-top NVIDIA Introduces DSX POD AI Factories to Accelerate Europe’s Infrastructure Deployment Factory-Built With a Global Ecosystem Including Bull, Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo, Schneider Electric and Vertiv, the New Reference Design Speeds Infrastructure Deployment From Months to Weeks, Accelerating Time to First Production Tokens October 21, 2026 News Summary: NVIDIA introduces DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners in modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. Factory-built units reduce deployment time at a prepared site from six months to as little as 14 days, helping customers begin generating production tokens and earning revenue sooner. A global ecosystem of computing and infrastructure partners are working with NVIDIA to deliver modular AI factories worldwide in early 2027. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today introduced DSX POD , a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. The units arrive ready to connect out of the box to a prepared site’s power, cooling, networking and other supporting infrastructure, reducing deployment time from six months to as little as 14 days. DSX POD moves the integration and installation of computing, networking, cabling, rack-level power and liquid cooling to the manufacturing facility, reducing the extensive planning, construction, specialized labor and logistics of a traditional onsite build. Factory-tested containers reduce exposure to component delays and costly, error-prone onsite work, creating a shorter path to model training and production inference so customers can begin generating tokens and earning revenue sooner. “An AI factory creates value when it starts producing tokens — not when construction is complete,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA DSX POD, we’re bringing factory-built precision and speed to AI infrastructure construction — reducing deployment time from months to weeks so customers can scale capacity and bring revenue-generating production online faster.” Factory-Built Infrastructure NVIDIA DSX POD brings Vera Rubin systems together with the infrastructure needed to operate them in repeatable, factory-built, containerized designs that partners can manufacture and deliver at scale. It carries forward the design philosophy of the broader NVIDIA DSX™ infrastructure platform , with a distinct architecture that integrates and validates systems in purpose-built containers before transport and deployment. Partners complete rack-to-rack cabling, wiring, piping and functional validation before shipment. This work takes place separately from site preparation, further shortening the time needed to bring new capacity online. That earlier start to production is the link between deployment speed and economics. Time to first token marks when a new AI factory begins running models to serve production workloads, giving operators the opportunity to put their infrastructure to work for customers sooner. Global Partner Ecosystem and Availability NVIDIA is working with Anduril, Armada , Bull, Crusoe , DayOne, Dell Technologies , Delta, Eaton, Foxconn (Ingrasys), GIGABYTE, HPE , Lenovo, Pegatron, Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT), Schneider Electric, Vertiv and Wistron to deliver DSX POD AI factories worldwide in early 2027. Press Release Share Tweet Twitter Share LinkedIn Share Facebook Email ic_arrow-back-to-top NVIDIA and Supply Chain Partners Expand Capacity to Accelerate AI Infrastructure Buildout New Capacity Agreements and Manufacturing Facilities to Support Volume Growth and Strengthen Supply Chain Resiliency October 21, 2026 News Summary: Substrate agreements with IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron Technology Corporation will, in aggregate, drive a 2.5x increase in capacity over the next three years. Amkor plans to increase its advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028. KYEC will build new facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. SPIL is targeting to increase its optical-engine capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced plans with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform. Working with Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and Unimicron Technology Corporation, NVIDIA is enabling new and existing suppliers to expand critical manufacturing capabilities across substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines, strengthening the resiliency and redundancy of NVIDIA’s global supply chain. “We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our supply chain partners are the world’s best manufacturers. I’m grateful they are expanding capacity around the globe to scale production and help us deliver the AI supercomputing systems powering this new industrial revolution.” Expanding Substrate Capacity to Support Volume Growth NVIDIA plans to increase substrate capacity for its products by 2.5x over the next three years. The agreements below will contribute to this capacity expansion, with more underway. Under an agreement signed and announced earlier this year by IBIDEN, NVIDIA is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance to support IBIDEN’s Ono Plant in Japan. The expansion targets capacity reaching 3x current levels at the plant, with additional capacity expected to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is joining NVIDIA’s substrate supply chain, bringing immediate capacity from its existing operations in South Korea. The collaboration also supports facility upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea. By 2028, production allocated to NVIDIA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ total annual package substrate production capacity. NVIDIA is supporting Unimicron’s KF substrate manufacturing expansion in Taiwan with a capacity reservation agreement. The expansion is expected to begin adding capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028. Scaling Advanced Packaging for Next-Generation Platforms NVIDIA and Amkor plan to expand advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, targeting a greater than 300% increase in interposer wafer capacity by the end of 2028. The planned capacity expansion, alongside Amkor’s development of new manufacturing facilities in South Korea, will support higher production volumes for NVIDIA’s current and next-generation platforms. Expanding Semiconductor Testing and Strengthening US Manufacturing NVIDIA expects its total semiconductor testing capacity to double from calendar 2026 to 2027, supported by buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan and Singapore. NVIDIA’s $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC will support new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027. In Singapore, expanded testing operations are expected to begin high-volume production in February 2027. Creating the Infrastructure for Co-Packaged Optics NVIDIA and SPIL plan to expand manufacturing capacity in Taiwan for optical engines used in co-packaged optics, supporting the growing connectivity requirements of large-scale computing infrastructure. The expansion targets an increase of 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028.
